english: Consider the curves $y=\sin^{-1}x$ and $y=\cos^{-1}x$, $0\le x\le 1$, where the inverse trigonometric functions take their principal values. Let $A_{1}$ be the area of the region bounded by these two curves and the line $x=1$, and let $A_{2}$ be the area of the region bounded by these two curves and the $y$-axis. Then the value of $A_{1}-A_{2}$ is ______.
hindi: वक्रों $y=\sin^{-1}x$ तथा $y=\cos^{-1}x$, $0\le x\le 1$, पर विचार कीजिए, जहाँ प्रतिलोम त्रिकोणमितीय फलन अपने मुख्य मान लेते हैं। माना कि $A_{1}$ इन दोनों वक्रों तथा रेखा $x=1$ द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल है, तथा $A_{2}$ इन दोनों वक्रों तथा $y$-अक्ष द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल है। तब $A_{1}-A_{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: The curves meet where $\sin^{-1}x=\cos^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, at $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$; $\cos^{-1}x-\sin^{-1}x$ is positive before it and negative after it.
solution_full: On $[0,1]$, $\sin^{-1}x$ increases from $0$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\cos^{-1}x$ decreases from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $0$. They are equal where $\sin^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ (since the sum is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$), i.e. at $P\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

So the difference $\cos^{-1}x-\sin^{-1}x$ changes sign at $x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$: the region with the $y$-axis lies over $\left[0,\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right]$ and the region with $x=1$ over $\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},1\right]$.

Vertical strips would need $\int\sin^{-1}x\,dx$; horizontal strips are simpler. Inverting: $y=\sin^{-1}x\Leftrightarrow x=\sin y$ and $y=\cos^{-1}x\Leftrightarrow x=\cos y$, $0\le y\le\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Region $A_{2}$ (left of both curves, right of the $y$-axis): for $0\le y\le\frac{\pi}{4}$ its horizontal strip is $0\le x\le\sin y$; for $\frac{\pi}{4}\le y\le\frac{\pi}{2}$ it is $0\le x\le\cos y$. $A_{2}=\left[-\cos y\right]_{0}^{\pi/4}+\left[\sin y\right]_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}=\left(1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)+\left(1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)=2-\sqrt2$.

Region $A_{1}$ (right of both curves, left of $x=1$): for $0\le y\le\frac{\pi}{4}$ the strip is $\cos y\le x\le 1$; for $\frac{\pi}{4}\le y\le\frac{\pi}{2}$ it is $\sin y\le x\le 1$. $A_{1}=\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)+\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\sqrt2$.

Check by the sign change: $A_{1}-A_{2}=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}(\sin^{-1}x-\cos^{-1}x)\,dx$, and $\int_{0}^{1}\sin^{-1}x\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-1$, $\int_{0}^{1}\cos^{-1}x\,dx=1$, which gives $\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2$ again.
originality_note: New: the two regions cut off by sin^-1 x and cos^-1 x against the y-axis and against x = 1 compared through their difference, which is the signed integral of the difference (way 5). Closest known: area between sin^-1 x, cos^-1 x and the x-axis. Different because: the two regions on either side of the crossing are compared and the y-strips handle each.

concept_use.Area bounded by a curve and the x-axis;: The difference sin^-1 x - cos^-1 x changes sign at 1/sqrt2, so the two areas come from opposite signs and A1 - A2 is its signed integral.
concept_use.Area bounded by two curves: A1 and A2 are each regions bounded by the two curves and a line (x = 1 or the y-axis).
concept_use.Area obtained by integrating with respec: Writing x = sin y and x = cos y and integrating horizontal strips for A1 and A2.
